hints: Look closely at what functional groups appear in Y, a ketone plus a carboxylic acid from a cyclic starting material suggests oxidative cleavage of a C=C bond.
Count carbons in Y and in each option, since strong oxidation does not lose carbon atoms the total must match.
Map the two C=O carbons in Y back together to reform the original double bond and see where the methyl groups must have been on the ring.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the reaction type**

Y is an open chain containing both a ketone and a carboxylic acid. This is the classic product of strong oxidative cleavage of a cyclic alkene.

Hot, concentrated $\text{MnO}_4^-$ breaks $\text{C}=\text{C}$ to $\text{C}=\text{O}$:
$$ \text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{CR}_2 \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{O} + \text{O}=\text{CR}_2 $$
And any aldehyde $\text{RCHO}$ formed is further oxidised to acid $\text{RCOOH}$.

**Use carbon counting to limit the ring size**

Count Y: $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOH}$.

The hexanoic acid backbone is 6 carbons plus one extra methyl branch, so 7 carbons in total. A dimethylcyclopentene has $5+2=7$ carbons, while a dimethylcyclohexene has $6+2=8$ carbons. So X must be a 5-membered ring.

**Match the substitution pattern**

For cleavage to give one ketone and one acid, the double bond must be trisubstituted.

$\text{R}_2\text{C}=$ gives ketone $\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{O}$, here $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-$, so that alkene carbon carried a methyl group. $\text{RCH}=$ gives acid $\text{RCOOH}$ after further oxidation, here $\text{HOOC}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-$, so the neighbouring ring carbon carried the second methyl group. That is exactly 1,3-dimethylcyclopent-1-ene.

options.A: 1,3-dimethylcyclopent-1-ene has 7 carbons. Oxidative cleavage of its trisubstituted C=C gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ at the methyl-substituted end and $\text{OHC}-$ at the other end, which oxidises further to $-\text{COOH}$. The three remaining ring carbons become $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-$, giving exactly $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOH}$, compound Y.
options.B: This is a cyclopentadiene with two C=C bonds. Strong oxidation would cleave both double bonds and break the molecule into three small fragments, not one single 7-carbon keto-acid. Students choosing this confuse a diene with a mono-ene.
options.C: This is a dimethylcyclohexene with 8 carbons total. Cleavage would give an 8-carbon product, one carbon too many for Y. It cannot lose a carbon in a single oxidative cleavage step.
options.D: This is 1,3-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene, also with 8 carbons. Even though the double bond is trisubstituted like in A, the six-membered ring gives a longer chain between the carbonyls, producing a 7-carbon backbone plus methyl, not the 6-carbon backbone of Y.
